solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pick up awful cheat, causing grief

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notices a dreadful swindler and is left heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' here means hear rather than lift; 'awful' gives TACHE, the anagram of the cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish, a close synonym for sorrow or grief.

clue.text: Heated chow, perhaps?

parts.note: heated means hot
a chow is a breed of dog, signalled by perhaps

explanation.surface: Is this warmed-up food, or a warm Chinese breed of dog?
explanation.walkthrough: 'chow' is also slang for food, so the whole clue reads as a hot snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a sausage in a bun, food served warm.

clue.text: Stagger out of a labyrinth

parts.note: a labyrinth is a maze

explanation.surface: Someone staggers out of a maze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' is the verb meaning astonish, not reel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish them, which is to amaze.

clue.text: Court official, man after gratuity

indicators.note: after places the word for man behind the word for gratuity

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity
to man a place is to staff it

explanation.surface: A court officer, a fellow chasing a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court officer, originally carrying a metal-tipped staff.

clue.text: Pick nuts and biscuits

parts.note: the pick or cream is the best of something
nuts and crackers both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Choose some nuts and a few biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: Cream crackers are plain, unsweetened British biscuits usually eaten with cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream crackers are a kind of dry savoury biscuit.

clue.text: Fair flat

explanation.surface: A fair, level apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means both equitable and smooth or level.

clue.text: Staff reminder, no parking at the front

indicators.note: no, with 'at the front', says the parking letter is dropped from the start of the word

parts.note: a prod is a nudge or reminder to do something
P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A note to staff saying the parking spaces out front are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no ... at the front' removes P from the start of PROD.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a straight stick or pole, which is what a staff is.

clue.text: Group of nesting birds in castle on European lines

parts.note: in chess the castle is also called a rook
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: Birds nest in a castle beside a European railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a colony of rooks, crows that breed in communal nests.

clue.text: German chap, one eating less?

definitions.meaning: a ... cuts down on food, the question mark flagging the play on the word

explanation.surface: A German man who is cutting back on food.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a diet, eating less, is a dieter; Dieter is also a German first name.

clue.text: Vagrant recalled heading for Portobello market

indicators.note: recalled is read as 'called back', so the word for market runs backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A homeless person remembered going to Portobello Road market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' acts on 'market', the word at the end, giving TRAM; Portobello Road in London has a famous street market.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer, so a vagrant.

clue.text: Looks round centre of Florence, not a pretty sight

parts.note: eyes as a verb means looks at
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the centre of an eight-letter word is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A tourist gazes around the heart of Florence and finds something ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like 'around', but gives the round letter O; the centre of FLORENCE is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, so it is no pretty sight.

clue.text: Money for extra work done ahead of season

parts.note: something done is over, finished
a season is a time of year

explanation.surface: Pay for additional hours worked before the busy period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead of' is a charade signal: the word for done comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is the extra pay earned for hours beyond the normal working day.

clue.text: Lake inside game reserve

indicators.note: inside says the answer lies within the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A lake set within a wildlife reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across gaME REserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a poetic or regional British word for a small lake or pond.

clue.text: VIPs with supporters in T-shirts?

indicators.note: in says the supporters go inside the shirts

parts.note: T-shirts are tops
a bra supports the bust

explanation.surface: Important people wearing supporters' T-shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is an idiom for the senior people in charge, originally military officers.

clue.text: Bid by Conservative for collection

parts.note: a bid is an offer
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician makes a bid to acquire a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The offertory is the church collection of money taken during a service.

clue.text: Persona non grata forbidden to go on pitch

indicators.note: in a down clue going on top places one piece above the other

parts.note: out means not allowed, as in that's out
to pitch is to throw, or cast

explanation.surface: An unwelcome person is barred from the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' is a throw, not a sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone rejected by society, unwelcome like a persona non grata.

clue.text: Illness of mother, noblewoman

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a lady is a noblewoman

explanation.surface: Mother, a titled lady, is unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is a disease or ailment.

clue.text: Notice express coming

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
to vent is to express a feeling

explanation.surface: A notice of a fast train due shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' suggests a fast train but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival, the coming of something.

clue.text: Stake required, unlimited

indicators.note: without limits, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: something required is wanted

explanation.surface: An unlimited stake must be put up.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake each player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Sheath found in taxi caught by southern poet

indicators.note: caught by says one piece is held inside the others

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern or south
a bard is a poet
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A sheath turns up in a cab, snatched by a poet from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' means the taxi is held between the southern letter and the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds a sword's blade.

clue.text: Top grade hotel in mountain area

indicators.note: in says the hotel letter sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
Hotel is H in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A first-class hotel in an alpine region.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first Greek letter, used as a mark for the best grade.

clue.text: Part of conservation area, an early centre of Christianity

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A protected area that was once an early Christian centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona, a Scottish island, was where St Columba founded a monastery in 563.

clue.text: Seaman, on his tod, finds shellfish

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
on his tod is British slang for alone, from rhyming slang Tod Sloan

explanation.surface: A lone sailor finds shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on his tod' is British slang meaning by himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail, an example of shellfish.

clue.text: Head leaving specimen, more than enough

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and leaving says it goes

parts.note: a sample is a specimen

explanation.surface: A boss leaves behind a specimen, which is plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head leaving' drops the S at the start of SAMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, exceeding what is needed.

clue.text: Last letters of Guy de Maupassant, until now!

indicators.note: last letters says to take the final letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The final letters of the French writer remain unread so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet in 'not yet' means up to the present time.

clue.text: Sit with Santa's new helper

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Sitting with Father Christmas is a new elf helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal; the apostrophe in Santa's is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is someone who aids another, a synonym of helper.
